verdict.headline: U.S.-Iran combat resumes in the Gulf, sending oil higher ahead of a pivotal jobs week
verdict.label: Step aside: Iran strikes resume (Brent ~$90, 4pts from regime trigger); Sep hike ~57%; AAPL Ternus Day 1 (-0.7% premarket); 30Y 5.21% (briefly touched 5.31% trigger); BTC $78.7K above $76.7K support; NFP Fri +475K est.
verdict.horizon: Through September 4 NFP; posture reset on September 16 FOMC outcome
verdict.rationale_short: Monday opens with two new macro overlays stacked on top of Friday's hawkish backdrop. First: the U.S. struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz overnight — the first publicly acknowledged U.S.-Iran military exchange since late July — with Iran retaliating against U.S. bases in Jordan. Brent has crossed $90/bbl, adding an oil-price inflation impulse to an already-stressed rate environment; the $94 Brent regime trigger is now 4pts away versus a prior cushion of ~6. Second: Tim Cook's 15-year Apple tenure ends today, with John Ternus officially becoming CEO on September 1. AAPL is -0.72% premarket (~$316.83), a muted initial reaction, but the hardware-first lens Ternus brings into September's annual product event is an execution risk the market will reprice on signal rather than announcement. These developments compound but do not yet transform Friday's posture: the 30Y yield touched 5.31% intraday last week — formally crossing the regime trigger — before closing at 5.21% on August 28. That intraday breach without a close confirmation means the trigger has not formally activated; it is, however, a warning shot with zero margin. September FOMC hike probability has softened to ~57% (from Friday's ~67%), reflecting partial post-Jackson Hole digestion — the directional signal remains hawkish but is less unanimous than it was 48 hours ago. The decisive data corridor begins today: Chicago PMI (9:45 ET), then ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS tomorrow (Sep 1), ADP Wednesday, ISM Services Thursday, and NFP Friday (consensus +475K, 5.1% unemployment). BTC at $78,652 is constructive — live support above $76,661 with the Bessent buyback program 9 days out (Sep 9). NVDA is +0.70% premarket at $219.07, partially recovering Friday's -4.3% sell-the-news; still below $220 structural support, making this a recovery attempt rather than a confirmed base. Step-aside posture is intact: the regime framework has not formally triggered, and the NFP print is the single most consequential data point before the September 16 FOMC. Adding risk exposure ahead of that combination — Iran oil shock, hot NFP tail, Canada tariffs Sep 8 — has an asymmetric cost structure that does not favor longs.

watchlist_mentions.note: ~$316.83 premarket (-0.72%). Tim Cook's 15-year tenure ends today; John Ternus officially becomes CEO September 1. The market reaction is muted — succession was announced in April — but Ternus is a hardware engineer, not a platform strategist, and AAPL's premium multiple rests on the AI services narrative. September's product event is Ternus' first major public test; street is watching for an AI platform vision or a hardware-cycle pivot. AAPL near $320 with a hardware-first executive taking the wheel during an AI-valuation era is a new uncertainty layer. History of planned megacap CEO handoffs shows Year 1 swings from -38% to +76%; hold, don't add, until Ternus signals strategic direction.

~$219.07 premarket (+0.70% from $217.55 close). Friday's -4.3% sell-the-news reversal is being partially recovered. Still structurally below $220 support; a sustained daily close above $220 is the signal the distribution was a single-session flush rather than the start of a deeper repricing. Next Blackwell read-through expected around AVGO earnings (~Sep 4-5). Setup unchanged: $220 is the bull/bear line.

$78,652 live (Crypto.com, 11:02 UTC). 24h range: $76,988-$79,409. The $76,661 Aug 24 structural support has held through Friday's session, the weekend, and today's overnight range. Bessent buyback program starts in 9 days (September 9). Two consecutive daily closes above $80K remains the bull re-entry criterion. A daily close below $76,661 is the exit signal. The Iran geopolitical variable is the new wildcard — BTC sometimes catches a flight-to-safety bid in geopolitical risk-off but can also sell with risk assets in sustained deleveraging.

Friday September 4, 8:30 ET. Consensus: +475K payrolls, 5.1% unemployment. Advance signals this week: Chicago PMI today (9:45 ET), ISM Manufacturing Sep 1 (10:00 ET), JOLTS Sep 1, ADP Wednesday (consensus ~400K private payrolls), ISM Services Thursday. The Iran oil shock adds a complication: if Brent stays above $90 through NFP week, the Fed's energy-inflation calculus tightens even on a soft labor market print. A sub-200K NFP is the only near-term catalyst that could materially reduce September hike probability and flip regime bias dovish.

~$395-405 (estimated; second Monday of the AI-competition repricing). No management walk-back has materialized. The AAPL leadership transition may briefly overshadow the SaaS sector story in the headlines, but the structural question — AI as substitute vs. AI as product — remains unresolved. CRM vs. INTU bifurcation (AI-as-product premium vs. AI-as-substitute discount) remains the key sector spread to monitor.

trade_setups.asset: 30Y yield — trigger briefly breached intraday; close above 5.30% is formal activation
trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y touched 5.31% intraday last week — formally crossing the 5.30% regime trigger — before closing at 5.21% on August 28. That intraday breach without a closing confirmation means the framework has not formally activated, but the cushion is zero. The Iran oil shock adds a new inflation input the bond market will price through this week's data corridor. A confirmed daily close at or above 5.30% converts step-aside to outright bearish — the first formal regime activation since the framework was constructed.
trade_setups.entry: A daily close at or above 5.30% on the 30Y formally activates the regime. Size into inverse duration (TBT, TMV, short TLT) on that trigger. Inverse signal: a post-NFP close at or below 5.10% would indicate the trigger is deactivating through the September FOMC window.
trade_setups.invalidation: NFP September 4 prints below 200K and 30Y closes at or below 5.10%.
trade_setups.horizon: Through September 4 NFP; hard reset September 16 FOMC.

trade_setups.asset: Brent crude — Iran escalation pushes oil toward regime threshold
trade_setups.thesis: Brent crossed $90/bbl on renewed U.S.-Iran strikes (Larak Island rocket launchers), now within 4pts of the $94 regime trigger. Prior cushion was ~6pts. If the Strait of Hormuz faces any physical supply disruption, Brent could move rapidly through $94. Oil above $94 would be the second regime indicator at trigger simultaneously with the 30Y — a multi-indicator regime breach converts step-aside to an unambiguous bearish read.
trade_setups.entry: Long energy (XLE, CVX, XOM) on any escalation news threatening physical supply. $92 Brent is the early warning level; $94 is regime activation.
trade_setups.invalidation: Iran-US diplomatic progress via Qatar mediation causes Brent to close below $87 for two consecutive sessions.

trade_setups.asset: BTC — $76,661 support holds through two retests; Bessent bid T-9 days
trade_setups.thesis: The $76,661 Aug 24 support has now been tested twice (weekend intraday low $76,864; today's 24h low $76,988) and held. The Bessent buyback program provides a structural demand backstop starting September 9. Two consecutive daily closes above $80K is the bull confirmation threshold. The Iran geopolitical variable is the key new input — a sustained risk-off deleveraging scenario is the primary downside risk to this setup.
trade_setups.entry: Hold above $76,661. Add aggressively on two consecutive daily closes above $80K.

bear_case: The bear pathway now has three simultaneous triggers where Friday had two. The added variable is Iran: if the Strait of Hormuz escalates from airstrikes to a naval supply disruption, Brent could break above $94 concurrent with the 30Y threatening 5.30% — activating two regime indicators simultaneously for the first time since the framework was constructed. This week's data stack amplifies the risk: a hot NFP print (above 400K) would lock in the September 16 FOMC hike and push 30Y through 5.30% in a formal close. Canada's $19.9B tariffs take effect September 8, four days after NFP, stacking an import-inflation impulse on top of the oil-price and labor-market inflation picture. In a combined scenario — Brent above $94 + NFP above 400K + Canada tariffs effective + 30Y closing above 5.30% — the framework registers a multi-indicator regime breach for the first time, and the posture conversion to outright bearish is the mechanical next step. SPX 7,500-7,600 by September 16 FOMC is the downside target under that scenario. Secondary bear inputs: AAPL under Ternus fails to articulate an AI platform vision at the September product event, converting a neutral transition overhang to active selling at peak-Cook multiple; INTU's AI-competition repricing spreads into ADSK, HUBS, and DOCN without being absorbed as idiosyncratic. Step-aside is the correct posture ahead of this conjunction — no single trigger alone is sufficient to flip the call, but two firing in the same NFP week would be.
